messages:
Samir (partnerships): Heads-up — AtlasCompute just returned the signed NDA for their new X1 edge boards. They want a short early-access window (2 weeks) for benchmarking + integration feedback. Can we run this as a compact preview?
Maya (platform-eng): Great. Do we have hardware arrival ETA and serial access details?
Samir (partnerships): Shipping 2 boards to our SF lab, ETA Wed next week. Atlas gave us console creds and a support contact (alex@atlascompute.io). NDA says telemetry allowed for perf/telemetry only.
Lee (infra): Need to confirm network segmentation and KMS handling before we touch them. We should treat these as private devices — VPC-only, no internet egress except to Atlas telemetry endpoints.
Emily (eng-ml): For benchmarks I suggest: 1) 1-shot/8-shot picobench across 1k prompts, 2) latency p50/p95 for 512/2048 tokens, 3) memory/KV cache profiling. Also want to run our Optimize profiler (low overhead).
Jordan (solutions): Would be good to exercise our SDK fallback routing (hosted -> dedicated -> atlas) in a canary route. We can validate graceful degradation when capacity is hit.
Maya (platform-eng): Agreed. Proposed plan: - Prep lab (segmented subnet + ssh jump host) - Install atlas drivers + fw v1.2.3 - Run smoke tests - Run benchmark battery (Emily's suite) - Telemetry collection + upload to secure S3 prefix
Lee (infra): Ops notes: use this jump host config (temporary):
```
# jump host firewall
allow from redwood-lab -> atlas-board:22,443
egress block all except atlas-telemetry.atlascompute.io:443
```
Also enable host-level auditd and disk encryption.
Emily (eng-ml): Telemetry format: we only need perf counters + model outputs hash. We'll strip any PII by default. Suggested probe config: `optimize.profiler --sample-rate=0.1 --kv=true --tokens=2048`.
Samir (partnerships): Legal flagged a single clause: Atlas wants to publish a short joint note saying "partnered on early perf signals" after the preview. Legal asked for copy review.
legal-bot: @Samir (partnerships) please upload NDA redline to /legal/reviews and tag legal@redwood.com. I will queue a 48h turnaround for marketing collateral.
Jordan (solutions): Timeline check — if boards arrive Wed, we can run smoke + bench Thu/Fri and share preliminary numbers Mon. Ready to commit to a 2-week locked preview window after that.
Maya (platform-eng): Resource ask: need one infra eng (Lee) + one runtime eng (Maya) + Emily for benchmarks. Also request 4 hours of solutions time (Jordan) to exercise SDK flows.
Lee (infra): I can own jump host and network. ETA: provisioning done Wed morning.
Emily (eng-ml): I'll prepare a prompt set aligned with our latency-sensitive customers (search, chat, rerank). Will publish prompt_set_v1.json to the secure bucket.
Samir (partnerships): Action items: 1) Lee: secure lab + jump host (due Wed 09:00) 2) Maya: install drivers/fw and smoke tests (Thu EOD) 3) Emily: bench suite + prompt_set (Thu EOD) 4) Jordan: SDK canary flow test (Fri) 5) Samir: coordinate Atlas comms + legal copy (ongoing).
Jordan (solutions): Quick question: do we allow a small external audience (1-2 Atlas engineers) to join the lab session for debugging?
Lee (infra): Fine if they use jump host with tied accounts and expire after session. Must be logged and recorded.
legal-bot: Note — external engineer access requires a 1-way NDA amendment. Samir please confirm with Atlas.
Samir (partnerships): I'll ask Atlas to sign the access amendment.
ops-bot: Deploy log: test-s3-bucket policy created at 1859001500 by Maya (platform-eng).
Maya (platform-eng): Also adding a short perf config snippet we should use across boards to keep results consistent:
```
REDWOOD_BENCH_ARGS="--batch-size 8 --prefill 4 --quantize auto --seed 42 --run-id atlas-x1-2026"
```
Please use same env for all runs.
Emily (eng-ml): Reminder — set random seed and log run metadata. I will compute deltas vs our baseline (dedicated-nv) and produce a short summary table.
Samir (partnerships): Marketing ask — atlas wants an embargoed summary we can share with partners after the window. Legal will need final copy. Keep any public claims conservative (latency within ~10% of baseline, etc.).
Jordan (solutions): If bench results look promising, do we want to include a short "integration guide" draft for Atlas marketplace listing?
Maya (platform-eng): Yes — a 1-page quickstart + our recommended runtime flags. I'll draft it during the window.
Lee (infra): Blocking risk: firmware 1.2.3 has known thermal throttling at sustained 90% util. We should schedule at most 2-hour continuous runs or use cool-down windows in our bench runner.
Emily (eng-ml): Noted — will shape workloads accordingly and log thermal events.
Samir (partnerships): Okay — next sync: quick check-in Friday 16:00 to review smoke results. If anything fails earlier ping #eng-oncall.
Jordan (solutions): ack.
Lee (infra): ack.
Maya (platform-eng): ack.
Emily (eng-ml): ack.
Samir (partnerships): Thanks team — I'll post Atlas' access details once courier confirms delivery.
